title: Efficient adsorption of tetracycline antibiotic on modified kaolin–alginate beads synthesized with acetic acid
content:
Abstract

This investigation focused on the retention of tetracycline (TC) on acid-treated kaolin, which was then shaped into beads using alginate. Characterization investigations of the synthesized adsorbent included determining the pHpzc. The FTIR study was applied to detect the main functional groups attached to the adsorbent. SEM images provided insights into the morphology of the materials before and after TC adsorption. The crystalline phases were examined through XRD. The textural features were assessed by BET technique. Thermal stability and decomposition patterns were investigated using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA/TDA). Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was conducted to identify the thermal transitions of the prepared materials. Adsorption efficacy was examined under different operational parameters. Batch experiments revealed that the prepared modified kaolin beads exhibited a strong affinity toward TC, reaching a maximum adsorption capacity of 285.87 mg·g−1. This performance was achieved under optimized conditions: pH 6, initial TC concentration: 10 mg. L−1, bead dose: 2 g. L−1, agitation speed: 200 rpm, and contact time: 200 min. The equilibrium and kinetic behavior were described by the Langmuir isotherm and pseudo-first-order kinetic model, respectively. The calculated parameter ΔG° remained negative over the investigated temperature range, indicating thus the effect of spontaneity of TC adsorption. The thermodynamic parameters further suggested an endothermic adsorption process. The reusability of the modified kaolin gelled beads was evaluated by successive adsorption- desorption cycles. The adsorption efficiency gradually decreased over the cycles, reaching its lowest value in the third cycle.
